subject.title: [Refactor] Extract canonical configuration validation from core to plugin boundaries

question: Should this issue be narrowed to specific residual schemas that still bypass existing manifest contracts, or should OpenClaw undertake a broader config-validator redesign?
rationale: Current architecture already provides plugin-owned schema contracts and registry composition, while a broader redesign would affect compatibility-sensitive startup and configuration behavior without a demonstrated user-facing defect.

options.title: Narrow to residual duplicates
options.body: Require a concrete inventory of current-main schemas that cannot use configSchema, configContracts, or channelConfigs, then refactor only those owner violations.

options.title: Approve broader redesign
options.body: Sponsor a coordinated validator redesign covering registry lifecycle, cold-start validation, schema export, diagnostics, migrations, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Close after audit
options.body: Close this issue if the named plugin schemas are already manifest-owned and no specific unsupported ownership gap remains.

recommendation.title: Narrow to residual duplicates
recommendation.body: Require a concrete inventory of current-main schemas that cannot use configSchema, configContracts, or channelConfigs, then refactor only those owner violations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and prior reviews connect this person most directly to plugin manifest contracts and configuration-boundary decisions.
